newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 7.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Friday's Daily Variety:

* NEW YORK - ITT Corp agreed to sell its half share in Madison Square Garden to partner Cablevision Systems for $650 million, giving the hotel conglomerate a $150 million profit on its 18-month investment. The deal also gives Cablevision, the nation's sixth-biggest cabler, outright control of the arena, the New York Knicks basketball and Rangers hockey pro sports teams and the MSG cable network. The sale is ITT's first step toward exiting the entertainment business, a move it made under pressure from a hostile $6.5 billion takeover bid launched by Hilton Hotels in late January.

* NEW YORK - David Westin, president of Disney-owned ABC Network president will succeed Roone Arledge as president of ABC News in a major management shift at the network. Arledge, 65, the legendary former ABC Sports executive who has run the news division for the past 20 years, is being bumped up to the new post of chairman in preparation for his eventual retirement, but said he'll retain active day-to-day management of the division and act as CEO in a partnership with Westin.

* HOLLYWOOD - March midseason madness continued as the premiere of the comedy "Temporarily Yours" by Westinghouse's CBS gave the web a lift while ABC's "Arsenio" posted decent numbers. For Wednesday night, Disney's ABC won in households with a 9.9 rating and 17 share, according to Nielsen. Despite the heavy competition from new midseason shows, News Corp's Fox managed to squeeze out a second-place finish in households with an 8.6/14 from "Beverly Hills, 90210" and "Party of Five" as well as a win in adults 18-49.

* HOLLYWOOD - During the 1997 American Film Market, which ended Thursday in Santa Monica, Miramax was selling "Rum Punch," Quentin Tarantino's next picture, defunct Turner Pictures International's $55,000 suite went to John Kluge's Metromedia Entertainment Group and buyers flocked to pick up rights to Jean Claude Van Damme's next action movie. However a combination of global economic and cultural factors slowed the action at the 18th annual film-licensing bazaar. The strong dollar appeared to have thinned traffic in the corridors of the Santa Monica Beach Hotel this year, especially at the low-budget end of the market.

* HOLLYWOOD - Robert Towne will receive the Writers Guild of America's 1997 Screen Laurel Award, the guild's highest honor for screenwriting. Towne won an original screenplay Oscar for "Chinatown" and also wronte "The Last Detail," "Personal Best," "Tequila Sunrise," "Days of Thunder" and "The Two Jakes."
